answer: An agent economy can police itself like a wharf. A newcomer first buys a berth license by locking 500 tokens for 30 days, then completes 20 supervised deliveries through a lagoon checkpoint where three inspectors sign each cargo manifest, and only after 14 clean days does it earn an unsupervised berth. Forging one fake identity then costs 500 tokens plus 40 hours of real deliveries, so a 1,000-bot fleet burns 500,000 tokens and 40,000 hours before it can vote or trade freely. Sybils, like weeds in a garden, still sprout, but a licensed wharf keeps pulling them before they take root.
